## Device fan limits and clearer room activity

### Fan speed belongs to the device

Minimum and maximum fan percentage now live on each supported device controller as **Fan · Minimum speed** and **Fan · Maximum speed**. The obsolete room speed editors are removed. Two fans in the same room can have independent limits, and devices use their own supported speed range.

Existing room limits remain a compatibility fallback until that device receives its own limits. Changing one device does not change the limits of another. Settings remain editable while a native command is awaiting feedback; changing a limit does not send a hardware command or acknowledge an outstanding one.

### Ordinary rooms do not need specialist comfort inputs

The optional ISO 7730 controls—activity (`met`), clothing (`clo`), air speed, radiant temperature source, and the PMV analysis switch—are disabled by default in ordinary rooms. Existing unused controls are migrated once while preserving their entity identities, names and stored settings. Explicit PMV users keep their controls, and later user enable/disable choices are respected.

Advanced users can enable **Advanced comfort (ISO 7730)** in Home Assistant's entity settings. Turning it on exposes the optional input controls; incomplete inputs remain reported as insufficient data. No activity, clothing or airflow values are guessed. Normal temperature targets, automatic comfort based on measured temperature/humidity, and PID do not require these specialist inputs.

### Room overview colours follow reported activity

Room, temperature, humidity and active-device icons now follow current native device reports:

| Activity | Colour |
| --- | --- |
| Heating | Orange |
| Cooling | Blue |
| Humidifying | Teal |
| Dehumidifying / DRY | Amber |
| Air filtration / fan running | Green |
| Ventilation | Cyan |
| Multiple activity types | Purple |
| Idle, off or no reported activity | Neutral grey |

Air-quality icons reflect applicable air-treatment activity. A filtration fan does not colour CO₂ as if it were ventilating. Native idle/off reports override selected modes, PID demand is not used as activity evidence, and an ON supply switch is not mistaken for a working appliance. Changes to native activity update the card even when the HEM controller state stays unchanged. Tooltips identify the activity in English, Greek and German.

The room overview retains its four uniformly sized readings and compact responsive layout. Beta111's directional PID target cutoff and the optional per-device 30-second setpoint sequence are preserved.

Update in HACS, restart Home Assistant and refresh the dashboard to load the new card.
